headline: One in 20 UK adults now pays for AI, a study of 14 million bank accounts finds
summary: Researchers tracked 14.2 million UK bank and card accounts and found 5.1% of adults paid for an AI tool in June 2026, with spending above £1 billion a year. Claude’s share of spending on direct subscriptions has jumped to 29%.
body: About one in 20 UK adults now pays for an AI tool such as ChatGPT or Claude. Researchers from the University of Warwick, the London School of Economics and Imperial Business School published the figure on Thursday 5 November, in a working paper built on anonymised records from 14.2 million UK bank and card accounts. By June 2026, 5.1% of adults, about 2.8 million people, held a paid AI subscription. By July, UK spending on AI was running at more than £1 billion a year.

Most people who try AI don’t pay for it. The researchers cite UK surveys showing 35% to 62% of adults have tried a generative AI tool, and estimate that roughly nine in ten of them have no paid subscription.

Paying users skew young, male and professional. Adults in their 20s are nearly six times as likely as over-60s to have paid for AI. Men are 27% more likely than women to hold a subscription, though the gap is shrinking among new subscribers. In London, 6.8% of adults pay, against 3.6% in the rest of Great Britain. Around 20% of IT professionals pay for AI, compared with under 3% of nurses and social care workers.

Claude has grown fast. Between December 2025 and July 2026, its share of spending on subscriptions paid directly to AI companies rose from 7.4% to 29.4%, while ChatGPT’s fell from 73.5% to 52.5%. ChatGPT keeps far more subscribers: 71.2% of people paying for a general AI assistant in July, against 27.1% for Claude.
do_this: Haven’t started? Try the free versions of ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini before you pay. The researchers call the leading free versions competent.

Already paying? Check your phone’s app store subscriptions as well as your bank statement. The researchers found about two-fifths of AI subscriptions go through app stores, where your statement may show only a generic app store charge.
source_name: the Who Pays for AI? working paper
